scope: Proposition 4.3 (Interior smearing moments) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a uniform height problem with boundary values bounded in absolute value by K. Let the center of a radius-a smearing have distance n from the boundary, with 1 ≤ a ≤ c0n for a sufficiently small fixed c0 > 0. Then, for every finite p, ∥ ∑ x wxH(x)∥Lp ≤ Cp ( 1 + √ log(n/a) ) . (4.4) Here Cp depends on p, A, K, but not on boundary regularity. The same statement holds for bounded data on the inner face chain of a dual cut, and in the bounded skeleton faces considered above.
